# Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna (Tha-Ap 20)

**ID:** Tha-Ap 20
**Section:** Therāpadāna (tha-ap)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

A full parallel to the poem is preserved later in the same collection as Tha-Ap 563 (*Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna*). The traditions regarding Raṭṭhapāla (Sanskrit: Rāṣṭrapāla) are widely represented across early Buddhist literature: the narrative figure corresponds to the protagonist of the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* (MN 82), with parallel traditions preserved in the Chinese Madhyama Āgama (MĀ 132), separate Chinese translations (T 68, T 69), the Sanskrit *Avadānaśataka* (Avs 90), fragments from the Turfan collection (SHT Sutta 18), and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D 1).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
